A reader who glances at the figure (or who sees only the figure, as in a slide or a skim) learns "many arrows vs few arrows," not "materialize-then-re-read vs never materialize."

figure: FIGURE 15.1 — FlashAttention: the same math, far less HBM traffic
issue: The BEFORE panel is annotated "O(L²) HBM traffic" while the AFTER panel carries no complexity label, which invites the false inference that FlashAttention is asymptotically cheaper in HBM traffic. It is not: with d fixed, naive attention is Θ(L²) HBM element-accesses and FlashAttention is Θ(L²d²/M) — the same order, with a constant-factor reduction set by on-chip SRAM capacity M. The caption's scope note ("the gain is fewer HBM round-trips, not a change to the attention mathematics") addresses the mathematics, not the asymptotics, so the misconception survives the caption. This is exactly the inference a reader is likely to carry into later capacity arithmetic.
evidence: Rendered page, PDF 257: BEFORE annotation "O(L²) HBM traffic: L×L intermediate written + every query re-reads the KV rows"; AFTER annotation "KV reused per tile — no single global K/V pass; no L×L intermediate in HBM" with no complexity term. Caption: "the gain is fewer HBM round-trips, not a change to the attention mathematics (floating-point caveat ...)" — no statement about asymptotic order.
acceptance_test: Add an explicit complexity qualifier to the AFTER panel, e.g. "Θ(L²) HBM accesses with a constant-factor reduction set by on-chip capacity (d²/M)" (or an equivalent statement in the caption). Acceptance: the figure cannot be read as claiming an asymptotic reduction in HBM traffic, and the phrase "constant factor" or "d²/M" appears somewhere in the figure or its caption.

figure: FIGURE 15.1 — FlashAttention: the same math, far less HBM traffic (AFTER panel)
issue: The AFTER panel draws exactly two green arrows (one up, one down) between HBM and on-chip, labelled "few HBM round-trips." A reader can reasonably take two arrows as a fixed count of two HBM transfers, which is not what FlashAttention does: the number of HBM reads scales with the number of (query-block, KV-block) tile pairs. The caption's scope note explicitly disclaims this ("it is not a guarantee that every K/V element is read exactly once globally across all query blocks"), but the figure itself carries no such qualifier — the qualifier lives only in prose, which is the wrong place for it given that the figure is the memorable artifact.
evidence: Rendered page, PDF 257: AFTER panel shows one upward and one downward green arrow between the "on-chip" and "Q/K/V HBM" boxes, with the label "few HBM round-trips" to the left. Caption: "Scope of the 'read once' claim: the tile-level on-chip reuse is per-tile; it is not a guarantee that every K/V element is read exactly once globally across all query blocks (the exact number of K/V re-reads depends on the tile schedule, and SRAM size ...)."
acceptance_test: Qualify the arrow count in the figure itself — e.g. label the arrows "per tile" or add "arrows = per-tile transfers; count scales with # (Q-block, KV-block) tile pairs." Acceptance: the figure alone cannot be read as asserting a fixed number of HBM transfers.
